entities.evidence: יַהְוֶה is the personal name in ‘Yahweh God.’ The one who clothes Adam and his wife is the same God who brought the woman to the man in Genesis 2:22.
לְאָדָם names Adam as a recipient of the tunics alongside his wife, Eve, whom he named in the preceding verse. The source tag identifies the same man.

review.translation: [Then|0] [Yahweh|1] [God|2] [made|0] [tunics of|5] [hide|6] [for Adam|3] [and his wife|4], [and he clothed them|7].

analysis.evidence: יַהְוֶה אֱלֹהִים is the subject, and כָּתְנוֹת עוֹר names what he made, tunics of skin. לְאָדָם וּלְאִשְׁתּוֹ identifies the recipients. The following verb וַיַּלְבִּשֵׁם describes how he then clothed them.
analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with prefixed וַ־ and no suffix

analysis.evidence: In וַיַּעַשׂ יַהְוֶה אֱלֹהִים, יַהְוֶה names the subject of וַיַּעַשׂ (‘made’), and אֱלֹהִים (‘God’) stands in apposition. Yahweh God made garments of skin for Adam and his wife.
analysis.morphology: Proper noun, masculine singular, with no prefix or suffix
analysis.sense: Personal name of the God of Israel

analysis.evidence: In יַהְוֶה אֱלֹהִים, אֱלֹהִים identifies Yahweh as God. Both וַיַּעַשׂ (“he made”) and וַיַּלְבִּשֵׁם (“he clothed them”) have a masculine singular subject.
analysis.morphology: Masculine plural absolute noun with singular reference.

analysis.evidence: The pointing לְאָדָם supports reading Adam as a name. The coordinated phrase וּלְאִשְׁתּוֹ, “and for his wife,” identifies the two people for whom God made garments.
analysis.morphology: Preposition לְ prefixed to a masculine singular personal name, without the definite article.

analysis.evidence: In לְאָדָם וּלְאִשְׁתּוֹ, the repeated לְ־ marks the man and his wife as the two recipients of the garments. The suffix ־וֹ refers back to אָדָם and identifies her as his wife.
analysis.morphology: Conjunction וּ־ ‘and’ + preposition לְ־ ‘for’ + feminine singular construct noun אִשְׁתּ־ + third-person masculine singular possessive suffix ־וֹ ‘his’.

draft.change: Add the Hebrew noun כֻּתֹּנֶת under כתנ with the sense “tunic.”
draft.definition: A tunic worn on the body.
draft.evidence: Genesis 3:21 identifies the tunics as clothing by describing their making and then saying that Yahweh God clothed the couple.

analysis.evidence: In כָּתְנוֹת עוֹר, the construct plural names the garments and עוֹר specifies their material, skin. Yahweh God makes them for Adam and his wife, and וַיַּלְבִּשֵׁם, “he clothed them,” confirms their use.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, feminine plural construct, with no prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: A tunic worn on the body.

analysis.evidence: In כָּתְנוֹת עוֹר, “tunics of hide,” כָּתְנוֹת is in the construct state and עוֹר names the material from which the tunics were made. The following וַיַּלְבִּשֵׁם means “and he clothed them.”
analysis.morphology: Common noun, masculine singular absolute, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: יַהְוֶה אֱלֹהִים is the subject of both verbs. He made כָּתְנוֹת עוֹר ‘tunics of skin’ for the man and his wife, and the plural object suffix on וַיַּלְבִּשֵׁם refers to the two people he clothed.
analysis.morphology: Hiphil wayyiqtol, third masculine singular, with prefixed וַ־ and a third masculine plural object suffix ־ֵם.
